knowledge_point.title: Computing an Integral Using the Sum and Constant Factor Rules

question.:question/worked-solution:
Using the sum and constant factor rules, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{2x^{4}+3}{x^{2}}\,\mathrm{d}x &= \int \left(2 x^{2} + \frac{3}{x^{2}}\right)\,\mathrm{d}x \\ &=2\int x^{2}\,\mathrm{d}x+3\int x^{-2}\,\mathrm{d}x \\ &=2\left(\frac{x^{3}}{3}\right)+3\left(\frac{x^{-1}}{-1}\right)+C \\ &=\frac{2x^{3}}{3}-\frac{3}{x}+C.\end{aligned}
$$
